bug_semantics: A producer can supply an otherwise validly signed JWS whose protected header contains `crit: ["x-custom-policy"]` and an extension such as `"x-custom-policy": "require-mfa"`. Before the fix, fast-jwt decoded the header, checked `alg` and the signature, then validated payload claims without interpreting or rejecting `crit`. The token was therefore accepted even though RFC 7515 §4.1.11 requires rejection when any listed critical extension is not understood and supported, enabling split-brain verification and bypass of extension-carried policy semantics.
flaw_origin: The flaw originated in fast-jwt's first verifier implementation: commit 51fe1ea3feacb931cd66b0f915b046cbeab88790 added `src/verifier.js` with a verification pipeline that trusted all decoded protected-header fields except those it explicitly checked (`alg`), and it provided no `crit` validation or supported-extension allowlist. This was an initial secure-failure omission, not a later regression, move, or refactor.
ai_marker: absent — the BIC commit object has author `Shogun <shogun@cowtech.it>` and committer `Shogun <shogun@cowtech.it>`, both dated 2020-01-15T18:44:15Z; its complete message is exactly `feat(wip): Initial version.` with no `Co-Authored-By`, `Generated-with`, or other AI trailer, and neither identity is a bot.
evidence: First-party advisory: https://github.com/nearform/fast-jwt/security/advisories/GHSA-hm7r-c7qw-ghp6 identifies CVE-2026-35042, describes acceptance of unknown `crit` extensions, cites RFC 7515 §4.1.11, and reports the npm affected range as `<= 6.1.0` (its `first_patched_version` field is null).

BIC commit and immutable source: https://github.com/nearform/fast-jwt/commit/51fe1ea3feacb931cd66b0f915b046cbeab88790 and https://github.com/nearform/fast-jwt/blob/51fe1ea3feacb931cd66b0f915b046cbeab88790/src/verifier.js#L13-L29 show the first `verifyAlgorithm` implementation; https://github.com/nearform/fast-jwt/blob/51fe1ea3feacb931cd66b0f915b046cbeab88790/src/verifier.js#L162-L224 shows decoded `{header,payload,signature}` flowing through algorithm/signature and payload checks with no inspection of `header.crit`. The commit adds `src/verifier.js` from `/dev/null`, so this is the smallest repository commit that first creates the vulnerable acceptance path.

Direct-parent verification: the BIC's commit object at https://api.github.com/repos/nearform/fast-jwt/git/commits/51fe1ea3feacb931cd66b0f915b046cbeab88790 gives the full parent `5063678a36ff118da9671f1f1df3d67cc95d1169`. The parent commit https://github.com/nearform/fast-jwt/commit/5063678a36ff118da9671f1f1df3d67cc95d1169 contains only the initial project/configuration/documentation/package files and no `src/` tree; requesting https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nearform/fast-jwt/5063678a36ff118da9671f1f1df3d67cc95d1169/src/verifier.js returns 404. Thus both `src/verifier.js` and the vulnerable verification path are absent in the immediate parent.

BIC-only attribution evidence: https://api.github.com/repos/nearform/fast-jwt/git/commits/51fe1ea3feacb931cd66b0f915b046cbeab88790 exposes the complete BIC commit object: human author and committer `Shogun <shogun@cowtech.it>`, message `feat(wip): Initial version.`, no trailers, and no bot identity. No PR, fix, branch, or later commit was used for attribution.

Affected-boundary evidence: packed tag refs resolve `v0.1.0` to `878469bd124161f35b43b38575f9d8a237c65061` and `v6.1.0` to `986a77a7d59964ad6eebe9de5681d9134cc435b4`. The first release page https://github.com/nearform/fast-jwt/releases/tag/v0.1.0 is later than the 2020-01-15 BIC, and the immutable v0.1.0 verifier at https://github.com/nearform/fast-jwt/blob/v0.1.0/src/verifier.js retains the no-`crit` pipeline. At the upper affected boundary, https://github.com/nearform/fast-jwt/blob/v6.1.0/src/verifier.js#L178-L229 likewise calls algorithm/signature and payload/claim checks without `validateCrit`, `allowedCritHeaders`, or any `header.crit` handling.

Direct-fix evidence: https://github.com/nearform/fast-jwt/commit/80b49c73cf708701e1e3da7c16ef735789cb269c (`fix acceptance of unknown crit headers and comply with RFC 7515 (#591)`) adds `validateCrit`, a registered-header deny set, secure-by-default `allowedCritHeaders`, presence/type/nonempty/duplicate checks, `FAST_JWT_INVALID_CRIT_HEADER`, and invokes validation in `verifyToken`; immutable fixed lines are at https://github.com/nearform/fast-jwt/blob/80b49c73cf708701e1e3da7c16ef735789cb269c/src/verifier.js#L174-L253. Searching its direct parent `597c4b6e6af3bd823f624debdaa7f57fa92b1e2d` for `validateCrit`, `allowedCritHeaders`, and `header.crit` produced no matches, while the fixed commit contains the validator and call.

Fixed-boundary evidence: the next release, v6.2.0, resolves to `e07b1fd23f02a47f1be677a21a4f07607b478e66`. https://github.com/nearform/fast-jwt/compare/v6.1.0...v6.2.0 lists direct fix `80b49c73cf708701e1e3da7c16ef735789cb269c`, and https://github.com/nearform/fast-jwt/releases/tag/v6.2.0 explicitly lists “fix acceptance of unknown crit headers and comply with RFC 7515” via PR #591. Thus repository history establishes v6.1.0 as vulnerable and v6.2.0 as the first release containing the fix, despite the advisory API's null `first_patched_version`.

Fix PR: https://github.com/nearform/fast-jwt/pull/591 states the RFC 7515 §4.1.11 problem, documents secure-by-default rejection of extensions not listed in `allowedCritHeaders`, and was merged as the direct fix commit above.
reasoning: Vulnerability-first tracing starts from the advisory's concrete failure: a valid signature does not make a JWS valid when its protected `crit` list names an extension the recipient does not understand. In the BIC, `createVerifier` decodes the token and the newly added verifier checks the algorithm, signature, and payload claims, but never examines `crit`; that omission is exactly what causes acceptance. History bottoms out at 51fe1ea3feacb931cd66b0f915b046cbeab88790 because it creates the verifier source and vulnerable pipeline, while its immediate parent has no `src` tree or verifier at all. The flaw is present in the first published v0.1.0 code and still present at the advisory's `<=6.1.0` upper boundary. Commit 80b49c73cf708701e1e3da7c16ef735789cb269c directly closes the path by rejecting malformed, unknown, duplicate, registered, or absent critical extensions and is included in v6.2.0. The BIC is an ordinary initial implementation commit with no reconstructable squash members. Under the required BIC-only attribution rule, its complete commit object contains only a human author/committer and a trailer-free message, so later activity is irrelevant and the causal verdict is NOT_AI.
